entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Raniero Capocci (Ranieri da Viterbo, d. 1250) was an Italian cardinal and political agent of the papacy in the age of Frederick II. A prominent member of the sacred college under popes such as Gregory IX and Innocent IV, he embodied the militant curial opposition to Hohenstaufen power in Italy—preaching, legating, and organising Guelf resistance.

His career shows how thirteenth-century cardinals were not only electors but field politicians: raising money, stirring cities, and framing the emperor as a persecutor of the Church. Viterbo and the Papal States formed the geographic base of such anti-imperial clerical networks.

Raniero remains a named face of the papal–Hohenstaufen struggle that defined Italy's Guelf–Ghibelline era.
